theme: The hidden cost of planning a corporate event without a production partner

linkedin.text:
An observation from 16 years of production briefs:

The companies that struggle most with corporate events are rarely the ones with the smallest budgets. They're the ones who treated event production as a task to delegate internally rather than a discipline that requires dedicated expertise.

Here's what that typically looks like in practice:
— The brief goes to someone who also has a full-time role
— Vendor negotiations happen without benchmark pricing knowledge
— The run-of-show gets written two weeks before the event
— Contingency planning is a single conversation, not a documented protocol

By the time things get complicated — and they always do — there's no experienced team to course-correct.

We've produced 1,500+ events across 130+ destinations. The organisations we work with most closely aren't the ones who can't run events. They're the ones who understand the difference between running an event and producing one.

If you're currently in scope conversations for a conference, product launch or incentive trip, I'm happy to share what a production-led brief looks like vs. a logistics one. Drop a comment or DM me. 🎯

The thing nobody tells you before planning a corporate event in-house:

The venue is 20% of the work.
The other 80% is the 47 things that can go wrong between 'confirmed' and 'doors open.'

After 1,500+ events across 130+ destinations, we know exactly which decisions get made too late, which vendors overpromise, and which moments on the run-of-show are always the riskiest.

That knowledge is the difference between an event people remember for the right reasons — and one the planning team never wants to repeat.

From business to pleasure — built on the details your internal team shouldn't have to learn the hard way. 📋✈️

facebook.text:
The thing nobody tells HR directors before they plan their first major conference in-house:

The venue costs are the easy part.

What actually eats the budget — and the team's sanity — is the 47 micro-decisions nobody saw coming. AV timing. Run-of-show gaps. Catering handoffs. Transfer logistics for 300 people. The keynote speaker who needs a specific setup that wasn't in the contract.

We've produced 1,500+ events across 130+ destinations for 25,000+ participants. The organisations that came to us after trying to run it internally almost always said the same thing: 'We didn't know what we didn't know.'

The second time, they called us first.

If you're in early planning on a conference, incentive trip or company event — we're happy to walk you through what the real scope looks like before you commit to anything. No pitch, just a conversation. 💬
